titulo: Roblox player uncovers cheating, awarded Guinness World Record

fuente.nota: Texto recortado por párrafos; sin cambios en las frases.

parrafos: In early January, international media reported that Quinten Delaere, an 18-year-old, had been officially recognized by Guinness World Records after exposing cheating on the Roblox platform. Delaere, known online as 'kannotlogin', used data analysis to demonstrate that the top times on the global leaderboard were achieved using illegal scripts.

Delaere was competing in a speed-running event for the game Ultimate Easy Obby. The event was an official collaboration between Roblox and Guinness World Records. Players had to complete a digital obstacle course as fast as possible. According to JV, after weeks of practice, Delaere posted a time of 5 minutes and 48.96 seconds. Before the competition closed, three unknown accounts posted times around 5 minutes and 42 seconds. JV reported that Delaere, posting on Reddit, believed the times were humanly impossible.

First, the analysis pointed to the timestamps of the badges earned by the rival accounts. The data showed that badges were unlocked in a non-chronological order. Delaere’s report described the non-chronological order as consistent with the use of teleportation scripts in a normally linear course.

Second, the top accounts were missing specific digital items in their inventory. Players who cross the finish line automatically receive a 'digital receipt' (an in-game item). The suspect accounts lacked this item. According to Kotaku, Delaere argued that "this proved he never actually touched the finish line trigger; he likely teleported a coordinate script to the end-game lobby."

PCGamesN reported that Delaere’s investigation found expired items in the players’ inventories. Delaere also submitted a frame-by-frame video analysis of his own run to calculate the theoretical maximum speed, arguing that the rival times were mathematically unachievable. "I took my best run and calculated the theoretical maximum time save possible (perfect pixels, zero drag). Even with a TAS (Tool-Assisted Speedrun) level of perfection, the times the cheaters posted were mathematically impossible within the game’s physics engine."

Delaere submitted his findings to the Guinness World Records headquarters in London. MeriStation reported that, after an internal review, the organization concluded Delaere was correct, disqualified the other accounts, and awarded him the official world record. The challenged times were removed from the database. The time set by Delaere was officially recognized as the new world record.
titulo_es: Un jugador de Roblox destapa trampas y recibe un récord Guinness
resumen_es: Un joven de 18 años demuestra con análisis de datos que los mejores tiempos de una competición de Roblox se lograron con trampas, y Guinness World Records acaba descalificando a los tramposos y reconociéndole el récord mundial.
nivel_motivo: Contiene jerga de videojuegos (speedrun, script, TAS), pero la sintaxis es clara y el razonamiento fácil de seguir: C1 se ajusta mejor que C2.

ideas_clave.idea: Guinness World Records officially recognised an 18-year-old player who used data analysis to prove that the fastest times on a Roblox leaderboard had been obtained with illegal scripts.
During an official Roblox-Guinness speedrunning contest on an obstacle course, three unknown accounts beat his time by about seven seconds, which he considered humanly impossible.
His analysis showed that the rival accounts had earned badges out of order and lacked the item given at the finish line, suggesting they had teleported instead of completing the course.
He also studied his own run frame by frame to calculate the fastest time theoretically possible and concluded that the rival times were mathematically unachievable.
After an internal review, Guinness agreed with him, disqualified the other accounts, removed their times and awarded him the world record.

resumen_modelo: The article reports that Guinness World Records has officially recognised Quinten Delaere, an 18-year-old gamer, after he exposed cheating in a speedrunning competition organised jointly with Roblox. Having completed the online obstacle course in just under six minutes, he noticed that three unknown accounts had posted times roughly seven seconds faster, which he regarded as impossible. To prove it, he gathered several pieces of evidence: the badges of those accounts had been unlocked in a non-chronological order, and they lacked the digital receipt awarded on crossing the finish line, which suggested the use of teleportation scripts. Furthermore, a frame-by-frame analysis of his own run showed that even a flawless performance could not match those times. Consequently, Guinness disqualified the suspect accounts and recognised his time as the new world record.
